subject: Computer Science

entities.name: Stack
entities.summary: A LIFO (last-in, first-out) collection: items are pushed onto and popped from the top.

atoms.statement: A stack removes the most recently added item first (LIFO).

questions.prompt: In which order does a stack remove its items?
questions.explanation: A stack is LIFO: push adds to the top and pop removes the top, so the newest item leaves first.

atoms.statement: Stacks back call/return, undo history and expression evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which task most naturally uses a stack?
questions.explanation: Undo restores the most recent action first — last-in, first-out, which is exactly a stack.

questions.prompt: Build a justification for using a stack to implement undo.
questions.explanation: A complete justification names the LIFO characteristic, ties it to undo restoring the most recent action, and notes a limitation.

payload.prompt: Select the parts that make one complete justification.

bank.text: A stack is LIFO, so the most recently added item is removed first
Undo must restore the action the user performed most recently
A stack only exposes its top, so you cannot jump straight to an arbitrary earlier action
It is simply faster than every other option
A stack always uses less memory than a queue

entities.name: Queue
entities.summary: A FIFO (first-in, first-out) collection: items join at the back and leave from the front.

atoms.statement: A queue removes the earliest added item first (FIFO).

questions.prompt: In which order does a queue remove its items?
questions.explanation: A queue is FIFO: items enqueue at the back and dequeue from the front, so the oldest item leaves first.

atoms.statement: Queues back print spooling, scheduling and buffering.

questions.prompt: Which task most naturally uses a queue?
questions.explanation: Print jobs are served in the order they arrived — first-in, first-out, which is a queue.

entities.name: Control loop
entities.summary: A closed control loop: a sensor measures, a processor decides, an actuator acts on the environment.

atoms.statement: A control loop flows sensor -> processor -> actuator.

questions.prompt: Rebuild a valid closed control loop.
questions.explanation: The sensor measures a value, the processor decides what to do, and the actuator carries out the action: sensor -> processor -> actuator.

payload.prompt: Arrange the pieces into a valid control flow.

confusionPairs.note: Both are linear collections, but a stack is LIFO and a queue is FIFO.
